questions.question: When is a port from one agent framework to another done?
options: When it makes the same tool calls with the same arguments on the same inputs as the old one
When the demo question gets a good answer
When the old code is deleted
questions.explanation: Behaviour lives in the tool calls. Compile success and one good answer don't prove it.

questions.question: In the camelCase bug, every tool call failed. What did the final answers show?
options: The target's answer was an error
Both answers were identical, so an answer-only check would have passed the broken port
questions.explanation: Models can report success they didn't achieve. Compare trajectories, not just answers.

questions.question: Why does the replay use follow_schema for the target run?
options: A real model reads the new schema and uses its parameter names, so the replay must too
questions.explanation: Without it, the replay would keep sending the old names and miss the schema change.

questions.question: The generated LangGraph code parsed with ast.parse but failed when imported. Why can that happen?
options: Parsing only checks syntax; undefined names and wrong imports appear only when the code is imported or run
questions.explanation: Syntax checks are a first gate. Import and run the generated code against the real library too.

questions.question: Replay parity passed, but the target framework adds 'reply with JSON only' to the system prompt. What next?
options: Run a small live evaluation, because replay can't show how a real model reacts to the extra instructions
questions.explanation: Replay fixes the model's replies; only a live run shows behavioural changes from prompt differences.

questions.question: LangGraph 1.x warns that create_react_agent moved to langchain.agents. What does this teach about ports?
options: APIs move between versions; pin versions and re-run parity after every framework upgrade
questions.explanation: An upgrade is a small port. The same parity suite protects it.
